newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbia parliament to discuss privatisation in July.
newsitem.headline: Serbia parliament to discuss privatisation in July.

text.p: Serbia's parliament will not discuss draft privatisation law today, Serbia's parliament speaker said on Monday.
The document was expected to come on the agenda later during the extraordinary session expected to last several days.

"The ownership transformation law is not on the agenda today. The law will be discussed later in the session. It is already in the parliament procedure, committees can discuss the draft... and when the government calls for a parliament session I will schedule it," Dragan Tomic told reporters.

Serbia's privatisation law is expected to clear path to changing ownership structure of medium and small firms while big state-owned enterprises will be transformed and privatised according to a special government programme.
The draft was first presented late in March and promised to be adopted by the end of June with implementation scheduled for July.
The heavily changed privatisation law is slated to become effective as of October 31. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
